summary: Implemented phase 6 of the 11-phase gate-framework refactor, closed cleanly and committed. Phase 6 enforced both previously-declared-but-unenforced timeout bounds: a new gate_registry_exec_bounded primitive (lib/gate-registry-lib.sh) runs each migrated gate under its registry timeout_s, killing the whole process group on expiry and reconciling CHECKS/FAILURES/FINDINGS_LIST/CURRENT_GATE back across the required subshell boundary via a declare -p dump/source roundtrip; run-all.sh gained a uniform RUN_ALL_SUITE_TIMEOUT_S (default 600s) applied identically in its sequential and parallel paths via `timeout -k 5`, recognizing timeout's bimodal 124/137 exit-status contract. Both bounds were proven to fire, name the right unit, and let the run reach a stable summary against deliberately-stalled fixtures. A full, un-scoped verify-deploy.sh run on an effectively-idle machine converged to exactly Phase 5's documented 5-suite failure set plus gate3/gate5/gate20's already-documented pre-existing findings -- zero new failures, zero bound trips. One real flake (an overly-broad leftover-process pattern match colliding with a concurrent sibling suite's identical fixture command) was caught and fixed during this phase's own verification. Paused at this clean phase boundary rather than opening Phase 7 (gate-level concurrency scheduler, which should extend this phase's subshell/capture/reconcile primitive rather than build a second one) given the real-world time already spent on this dispatch.
